overall: Los Angeles is currently experiencing a classic late-June marine layer pattern, with overnight temps sitting at 62.6°F (running max as of ~9:55 PM PDT June 24) and patchy fog expected to persist through mid-morning. Conditions are cool and mostly cloudy with light southwest winds, consistent with a typical 'June Gloom' setup. No severe or tropical weather is impacting the LA basin directly — active alerts are confined to inland desert zones, eastern Kern County, and areas well outside the metro.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models are in unusually tight agreement: ECMWF=68.3°F, HRRR=68.4°F, and NBM=67.0°F, with only ~1.4°F spread across all three — a strong signal for a mild high. The NWS official forecast of 69°F aligns closely with this cluster. The morning fog and marine layer are well-captured by the models and will suppress early warming, but partial afternoon sun should still allow temperatures to climb to the upper 60s.
max_temp_prediction: The convergence of all three NWP models between 67–68.5°F, supported by the NWS 69°F forecast and the INTRADAY bucket distribution peaking at the 68–69°F bucket (13.3%), points to a high in the 68–69°F range. The persistent marine influence and partly sunny (rather than fully sunny) afternoon conditions slightly favor the lower end of that range, near 68°F. Confidence is moderately high given strong model agreement, though the wide spread in the intraday distribution (notable probability from 64°F to 79°F) reflects some residual uncertainty about cloud burn-off timing.
